independence: The reviewer authored earlier grammar-reference fixes only, and did not author any of the vocabulary or main 8A changes reviewed here.
review_method: All assigned saved-PDF PNGs personally viewed at full page resolution, 120 dpi. This was a visual and content review of the actual saved export, not solely an HTML or contact-sheet review.

scope_review.relationship: The changed banks now extend the main lesson starter selection with useful, bounded A1 topic vocabulary, while preserving the adjacent original practice activities. They do not require pushing the fuller list back into the main lesson.
scope_review.coherent_closed_sets: The complete alphabet, zero-to-one-hundred number support, seven weekdays, twelve months and thirty-one date ordinals appropriately remain coherent reference sets rather than being artificially withheld.
scope_review.vocabulary_meaning_support: Added items use pictures, short lexical meaning cues, concrete collocations or examples. These lexical definitions are appropriate support and are not compressed grammar-rule prose.
scope_review.grammar_inflation: No need to introduce unrelated or advanced grammatical systems was inferred from the vocabulary expansion.

critical_8a_review.main_67: The six core travel chunks and Toronto context remain usable, with a whole skyline/ferry photograph and intact contextual text.
critical_8a_review.main_68: Five large starter cutouts are clearly distinguishable: duck, squirrel, raccoon, beaver and goose. The More animals link sends learners to Vocabulary - Animals, page 141. The itinerary and writing spaces remain intact.
critical_8a_review.bank_141_animals: All twelve animals are pictured and labeled, grouped as wildlife (duck, squirrel, raccoon, beaver, goose), pets (cat, dog, rabbit, fish) and farm animals (horse, cow, sheep). The seven additional animals extend the main lesson without crowding its five starter pictures.
critical_8a_review.bank_141_travel: Six additional travel chunks are supported by aligned meaning cues: book a room, pack a bag, buy a ticket, catch a bus, get on a bus and get off a bus. The last two have clear into/leave meanings.
critical_8a_review.practice_142: Travel repair and open three-chunk production remain distinct from the bank. The wildlife picture/crossword and cover-and-recall task provide fresh practice; the recall instruction can use animals outside the crossword. Cells, instructions and writing lines are unobstructed.
critical_8a_review.animal_audio_reference: The full animals bank visibly carries audio tag 8.13. This review did not independently listen to the audio.

page_group_findings.finding: Unit 1 banks retain usable alphabet/number/country foundations and add supported greetings, personal-information fields, jobs and adjective contrasts. The original clue/card tasks and reserved QR area fit.

Unit 2 additions include six clear new personal-item pictures, correct digital quarter/half-hour examples, extended family meanings, pink and purple paint cutouts and long/short name models. Existing games and responses remain readable.

Routine banks now include read a book, listen to music and sleep; the weekday bank remains a complete seven-day set; place adjectives use simple concrete models. Secret-plan writing space and Unit 3 QR reserve remain free.

Food additions are large identifiable cutouts with aligned labels. Bitter/delicious have clear meanings. Peel/boil/fry/bake have four distinct picture models. Sharing-food extension and fresh repair/message tasks fit without reducing writing or QR space.

Six extra clothes are clearly pictured and labeled. Additional shopping verbs, store types and checkout objects have concrete models or meaning cues. Suitcase/clue tasks and decision-trail responses remain usable.

Additional places, home furniture/rooms, direction requests and day-out venues are A1-relevant and supported. Page 133 route images distinguish along/across/through/past. Page 134 keeps two full response lines clear of its QR reserve.

Past-time extension, complete date sets, music instruments and additional everyday irregulars remain legible. Page 139 explicitly distinguishes read /ri:d/ from past read /red/ and supplies a full past example. Next and Later have concrete event examples.

Cool/warm form a readable temperature progression, with wet/dry supported by meanings. Face/neck labels point to distinct features. Complaint cutouts clearly match head/stomach/foot messages, and earache/fever/I feel sick expand the bank. Added phone repair phrases fit above the ticket practice; all response lines remain clear.

layout_review.text_and_picture_labels: PASS - no clipping, overlapping labels or materially illegible additions found in these thirty-six full-page saved-PDF views.
layout_review.image_identification: PASS - added vocabulary pictures and the main 8A cutouts have usable size and whole identifiable subjects.
layout_review.writing_and_game_spaces: PASS - existing lines, boxes, crossword cells and clue-answer spaces remain usable and unobstructed.
layout_review.blooket_qr_reserves: PASS - visible reserved blocks remain clear, including the tighter page 134 arrangement.
layout_review.reference_adjacency: PASS - bank-to-practice page cues and the adjacent practice continuations viewed here remain coherent.
layout_review.identity_and_scope: PASS - the existing lesson headers, code tabs, bank styling and original practice framework remain intact; this pass does not impose a separate visual series.

limitations: Independent review covered the thirty-six assigned saved-PDF pages, not a new whole-book visual proof of every unmodified page.
This was a visual/content proof, not a fresh audio listening test or browser/PDF hyperlink click audit.
Prior grammar-reference edits by this reviewer are excluded from this independent vocabulary acceptance.
